slides.title: The big idea
slides.html:
Now we can prove the Unit 2 constructions.

Perpendicular bisector: the arcs from A and B have equal radius, so the crossing points P and Q have PA = PB and QA = QB. Triangles APQ and BPQ are congruent by SSS, so angle APM = angle BPM. Then triangles APM and BPM are congruent by SAS, giving AM = BM and equal angles at M that form a linear pair, so each is 90 degrees.

Angle bisector and angle copy: the equal arcs make two triangles congruent by SSS, and CPCTC gives the equal angles.
